title: A lasting economy level in the state, value iteration on r15
question: With the economy weight as a lasting level in the state (one step down / stay / up per turn), does value iteration find when to invest less in economy, and does that beat r15?
change: Action set econ5: the base bot's build factor at x0.25, x0.5, x0.75, x1 or x1.5, held between turns and moved one step at most per turn, from x1; value iteration over (turn, level) and (turn, level, income bucket).
method: 300k games with a random walk over the levels; value iteration for both state versions and min-count 20, 100, 500; min-count chosen per version on 2,000 validation seeds; both chosen policies on the 10,000 evaluation seeds against r15 and against a hand schedule (x0.5 from turn 16)
setups: Perfection, 16×16 continents, 4 players, Crazy, seat 0 Xin-Xi (human seat), learner base greedy-full-probe-perf-r15; opponents greedy-full-probe-perf-r15, greedy-full-probe-perf, greedy-full-probe-perf (anchor), seats shuffled per seed (rl-gate defaults from 27 Nov)
